body.statement: Fix any enrollment position, arm, schedule \(Y\), and predictable event \(E\in H_{bi}\). The event's contribution to the average inverse-propensity factor is exactly \(\mathbb E_{\mathcal D,Y}[\mathbf 1_E\{1-p_{bi}(z\mid H_{bi})\}/p_{bi}(z\mid H_{bi})]\). If \(P^O_{\mathcal D,Y}(E)\le\epsilon\) and \(p_{bi}(z\mid H_{bi})\ge\delta\) on \(E\), this contribution is at most \(\epsilon(1-\delta)/\delta\). Thus a rare \(\epsilon\)-probability branch is charged through its assignment probability rather than by the worst-path factor \(1/\delta\) alone.
body.justification: This calculation is the required low-propensity audit and prevents an information lower bound from treating negligible histories as certain.
body.gap: Worst-path martingale bounds are valid for coverage but do not by themselves characterize worst-case expected length under adaptive randomization.
body.consumer: It tells trial software how rare adaptive branches enter the borrowing penalty and guards against severe overconservatism.
